extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers and computational social scientists interested in automated news credibility, fact-checking, and media bias (Portuguese/Brazil focus)
extracted.subtask_description: Developing and evaluating models to predict sentence-level factuality in news reporting and the political/media bias of outlets, using a labeled dataset (FactNews) and features such as subjectivity, impartiality, emotion, and sentence length. Results are intended to be aggregated to assess overall source reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence-level factuality
rubrics_metrics.description: Predicting sentence-level factuality of news reporting. Sentences in the FactNews dataset are expertly annotated according to factuality definitions proposed by AllSides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a primary classification target for automated news credibility and fact-checking; annotations follow AllSides definitions. The paper frames this as one of two text classification problems and uses sentence-level labels to train/evaluate models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media outlet bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Predicting bias of media outlets (political/media bias) by analyzing sentences and aggregating predictions to the source level. Bias annotations in FactNews follow AllSides definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulated as a separate text classification problem; sentence-level biased labels are used to assess overall reliability of news sources by aggregation across sentences.

rubrics_metrics.name: FactNews dataset characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: A large sentence-level dataset titled 'FactNews', composed of 6,191 sentences expertly annotated according to factuality and media bias definitions proposed by AllSides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dataset scope and provenance are part of evaluation: size (6,191 sentences), expert annotation, and labeling scheme (AllSides) are central to training and benchmarking models. The dataset and baseline are provided for Brazilian Portuguese.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulation as two text classification tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: The problem is formalized as two text classification tasks: (1) predicting sentence-level factuality and (2) predicting bias of media outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design models and experiments around these two supervised classification tasks; use sentence-level labels for factuality and bias and aggregate outputs to evaluate source-level reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence length (word count) as a feature
rubrics_metrics.description: Biased sentences present a higher number of words compared to factual sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sentence word count can be used as a discriminative feature for separating biased from factual sentences; include length-based features in models or analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotionality / predominance of emotions
rubrics_metrics.description: Biased sentences have a predominance of emotions compared to factual sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emotion-related features or emotion-detection signals (e.g., lexicons, affective classifiers) are useful predictors for bias; consider modeling emotionality when predicting bias or factuality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fine-grained analysis of subjectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjectivity of news articles/sentences is an important dimension for predicting reliability and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform fine-grained subjectivity analysis (sentence-level) as part of feature engineering or evaluation; subjectivity measures provided promising results for predicting media outlet reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fine-grained analysis of impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Impartiality (degree of neutrality) is a complementary fine-grained dimension relevant to reliability and bias prediction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure impartiality at sentence level alongside subjectivity; use these signals to improve predictions of outlet reliability and bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregating sentence-level predictions to assess source reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the overall reliability of news sources by aggregating sentence-level factuality and bias predictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use per-sentence classification outputs to compute source-level metrics (e.g., proportion of factual vs. biased sentences) to rank or evaluate media outlets' reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portuguese / Brazil-specific focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Dataset and baseline are proposed for Brazilian Portuguese due to the severity of fake news and political polarization in Brazil and the lack of existing research for Portuguese.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying models or datasets, account for language-specific phenomena (Brazilian Portuguese) and the sociopolitical context; replicability and evaluation should target Portuguese-language news.
